title: 🚀  TDD, Where Did It All Go Wrong (Ian Cooper)
summary: Ian Cooper argues TDD went wrong when teams tested methods and mocked every dependency; he reboots it as testing behaviours through a module's public API with red-green-refactor and ports-and-adapters.

assertions.quote: all these tests with mocks they broke and we had to rewrite all the mocks

verdicts.note: Over-specified interaction tests are a documented cause of fragile suites in both practitioner literature and studies of test co-evolution.

assertions.quote: we were you know twenty to fifty percent slower than we had been before by writing tests

verdicts.note: Controlled studies of TDD report roughly fifteen to thirty-five percent more initial development time alongside fewer defects, so the slowdown is real but is partly repaid later.

Elite performers report far more automated testing than low performers (87% vs 57% automated unit tests, 58% vs 28% acceptance tests) while deploying 208 times more often with shorter lead times, so at the delivery level testing is associated with faster, not slower, delivery; the data are cross-sectional self-reports and do not isolate per-feature development time.

assertions.quote: the unit of isolation is the test not the thing under test

verdicts.note: A definitional reading of Kent Beck's book rather than an empirical claim.

assertions.quote: the customers never really looked at this stuff right

verdicts.note: Practitioner consensus including the Fit author's own retraction supports this, though some teams report value from Gherkin-style specs; no controlled study exists.

assertions.quote: for this brief moment speed Trump's design I want to get there as fast as I can

verdicts.note: Kent Beck's original claim, consistent with cognitive-load arguments against solving and designing at once, but not directly measured.

assertions.quote: when you refactor and this is the really important part you do not write any new tests

verdicts.note: Practice advice that follows from the definition of refactoring; whether existing tests actually cover the behaviour is case by case.

assertions.quote: at the end of that process delete the tests the tests help guide you but now they're a burden to somebody else

verdicts.note: A judgment about test maintenance trade-offs with no empirical comparison.

assertions.quote: the tools all break because I changed the way that my widgets work

verdicts.note: Flaky and brittle UI tests are extensively documented in industry reports and flaky-test research, which is why the test pyramid pushes coverage downward.
